coverage-addition-8.scope: Two unchanged original Thread-Metric IRQ bodies, three fresh KVM guests each, one 30-s window each. coverage-addition-9.scope: Original Zephyr v3.7 synchronous TCP/UDP upload bodies, three independent resets per protocol, 60 s, 16384/1024-byte payloads and original receiver/wire accounting. RIOT native priority threads, POSIX/lwIP, 65536-byte network heap and tickless native clock with 10-ms statistic grid; separate matched native-select timeout control. UDP maps blocking send to repeated native send calls only on transient buffer exhaustion, with a 2-s per-call guard and explicit wait accounting included in the original duration. TCP keeps its previously acquired firmware and one prior sample; UDP uses its separately bound adapter image. This is adapter-inclusive execution coverage, not an unmodified native-API performance score.

coverage-addition-10.scope: All 24 unchanged Zephyr v3.7.0 kernel-mode semaphore tests pass in one complete B1 reset; 28 real CPU_FROM_CPU2 IRQs. Native FreeRTOS counting semaphores, priority/FIFO waits and ISR operations; reset uses native abort-delay, byte pipe uses native queues plus writer mutex, actual worker stacks 4096 B. Native conditions 240 MHz, one core, 100 Hz; no skipped kernel-mode case. Adapter-inclusive correctness coverage, not a precision estimate, Zephyr userspace or leaderboard score.

coverage-addition-11.scope: All 24 unchanged Zephyr v3.7.0 kernel-mode semaphore tests pass in one complete B1 reset; 28 real CPU_FROM_CPU2 IRQs. Native RIOT semaphores, mutex priority waiters, native deadlines and IRQ-safe operations; reset cancels retired native instances with sema_destroy, bounded byte pipe uses native semaphore notifications. Actual worker stacks 4096 B, 240 MHz, one core; tickless native ztimer; no skipped kernel-mode case. Adapter-inclusive correctness coverage, not a precision estimate, Zephyr userspace or leaderboard score.

coverage-addition-12.scope: All 24 unchanged Zephyr v3.7.0 kernel-mode semaphore tests pass in one complete B1 reset; 28 real CPU_FROM_CPU2 IRQs. Native NuttX task groups and priority semaphore waits, native deadlines and IRQ-safe try/post; reset releases retired native semaphore instances with native posts, bounded byte pipe uses native semaphores. Actual worker stacks 4096 B, 240 MHz, one core; 100 Hz; no skipped kernel-mode case. Adapter-inclusive correctness coverage, not a precision estimate, Zephyr userspace or leaderboard score.

coverage-addition-13.scope: All 24 unchanged Zephyr v3.7.0 kernel-mode semaphore tests pass in one complete B1 reset; 28 real CPU_FROM_CPU2 IRQs. Native Rhino priority tasks and semaphores, native sleep and reset cancellation by retiring deleted static objects. Public take rejects ISR context; the no-wait compatibility operation reads/decrements the native object count under CPU IRQ lock, without faking interrupt context. Byte pipe uses native semaphore notifications. Actual worker stacks 4096 B, 240 MHz, one core; 100 Hz; no skipped kernel-mode case. Adapter-inclusive correctness coverage, not a precision estimate, Zephyr userspace or leaderboard score.

coverage-addition-14.scope: 24 unchanged Zephyr 3.7.0 kernel-mode cases, one complete one-vCPU 128-MiB Pi4B KVM guest, 28 real GICv2 SGIs. Native Tenon priority tasks, semaphore waits and timers. Explicit isolated-kernel compatibility fixes cancel the timeout on ISR wake and avoid duplicate wake-all transitions; original scheduler assertions and failed v1-v4 remain. Retired native objects map reset cancellation; byte pipe uses native semaphores, workers 16384 B. Correctness execution coverage of this fixed variant, not unmodified upstream capability, RAM/latency or B1 scores.

coverage-addition-15.scope: One complete native Tenon Pi4B one-vCPU 128-MiB KVM PH3 guest; unchanged SEI-derived C workload and contiguous 10-second PH3 steps to first loss. Baseline and integer workload increment are fixed from pre-trial calibration at 20% and 2.5% targets per SEI section 5.2; no post-result selection. Native priority tasks, semaphores and tick sleeps, fixed static OpenLibm. Native clock resolution is separately declared; no ESP32 or common-task score claim.

coverage-addition-16.scope: Three unchanged original Thread-Metric bodies; Tenon native tasks, semaphore and mailbox. New message image copies four native 64-bit words through two native try-operation mailboxes and owned buffers. Old custom-ring message diagnostics remain excluded. Existing valid preemption and semaphore images are reused; this is execution coverage, not an ESP32 score.

coverage-addition-17.scope: Native guest execution coverage of unchanged Zephyr 3.7 synchronous zperf cores, not bare original Tenon networking support or B1 score. lwIP dependency and API adaptation added; isolated previously qualified wakeup/timeout fixes retained. Native coarse UDP pacing and receiver versions explicitly reported. Prior Linux-socket RPC and malformed-ACK cohorts remain excluded.

coverage-addition-18.scope: Unchanged original TCP/UDP core execution on explicit Contiki native/Linux configuration. A bounded socket facade preserves native uIP ownership and runs the original platform loop while blocked, with point-to-point neighbor autofill and link-sized TCP segments. No FreeRTOS/IDF data sockets or replacement scheduler. Different target, not an ESP32 score; old hosted captures remain excluded.

contiki-native-subset-applicability.scope: Seven unchanged original counter cases, three fresh processes. The compatibility layer supplies count limit, validation, reset and return-code mapping; native PT_SEM performs init, count, signal and immediately available take. No blocking, priority, IRQ or full-suite conformance. The other original subsets require stackful priority threads absent from this frozen model. Native hardware interrupts are not equated with priority-thread scheduling. All 70 cells and original test denominators remain.

contiki-native-timeout-extension.scope: Three original single-caller timeout cases. The compatibility facade retains the original C call stack outside process callbacks and pumps precisely the original native event-loop iteration. Contiki etimer and process protothreads implement the wait; PT_SEM implements counters and available takes. Finite timeouts round up by one native tick. No host semaphore, priority thread or multi-waiter queue; original busy-wait(1 us) rounds up to the native clock granularity. Native/Linux execution, not B1 timing or ranking. Seven counter cases reuse their original three process captures; no duplicate measurement. Ten of twenty-four cases across two images, not a full-suite execution.

contiki-native-hardware-irq-counter-exte.scope: ESP32 B1 hardware CPU_FROM_CPU2 interrupts. Original C calls execute inside an unchanged Contiki process callback; semaphore counters and available takes use PT_SEM. IDF/FreeRTOS supplies boot, interrupt registration and ISR-context witness, not the tested semaphore or thread service. No stackful worker, host wait or preemption claim. Ten other cases reuse their archived Linux captures across two images. Thirteen partial cases across three images and two declared platforms, not a full-suite execution or a leaderboard input.

contiki-remaining-semaphore-semantics.scope: All eleven original bodies reach a rejected unsupported service in an actual native Contiki process. These are fail-closed controls, not proof of a semaphore runtime failure or an implementation of the missing worker service. Source/helper paths and the frozen execution model establish the compatibility gap. Existing thirteen positive cases are reused without reruns.

contiki-native-mt-sem24-extension.scope: Separately implemented Contiki-NG MT extension on bare STM32F407; not unchanged Contiki-NG, ESP32 B1, or a leaderboard input
